loss.phase: First orbit-average phase. sim.c and slurm-7132.out identify the Loss cone multiplier.
loss.quantity: Cellwise-constant ion distribution time-derivative multiplier, nodal order 0. 1 = evolve (all corners trapped), 0 = hold (at least one corner reaches a wall).
loss.sampling: Three unfiltered native cuts in (signed v_parallel, mu). Each mask[im][iv] character is the exact bit at (iz,iv,im). Z[m], v_parallel[m/s], mu[keV/T].
loss.linked_probe: Every one of the 6,144 cells on the three cuts can be selected. Bounds use the stitched physical map edges. Computations use both incident native velocity-map traces and the saved mass via kinetic_kev_per_v2 = m_i/(2 keV in joules). The reference SHA-256 covers 6,144 bytes in [slice,iv,im] order, one trapped bit per corner.
loss.cut_cell: Inner slope, (iz,iv,im)=(291,37,11). Only corner 1 is trapped. The other seven can reach a wall, so the saved flag is passing (0). On the lower axial face the Hamiltonian-trapped region covers about 17.24% of the physical velocity-cell area (trapezoidal integration of the critical speed at 1,001 moment samples).
loss.beam_well: Midplane, (iz,iv,im)=(200,32,0). All eight corners are trapped. Corner 2 has zero magnetic moment to roundoff and turns on both electrostatic shoulders. Off-centre density peaks near the injected beams’ turning points produce the well, as described in Chapter Gkeyll POA simulations/tex-files/results_lorentzian.tex.
loss.profiles: Flattened left and right P1 traces in increasing Z, both field traces kept at shared faces. Static physical Z and magnetic field B[T] from geometry frame 0 (0 s), q_i phi[keV] from the frame-2 DG electrostatic potential. The run-wide velocity map stores no frame or time. Modal endpoint values are c0/sqrt(2) +/- sqrt(3/2) c1.
loss.classifier: H = m_i v_parallel^2/2 + mu B + q_i phi. Use piecewise-linear U=mu B + q_i phi. Take its maximum on each path, including its launch point, both DG traces, and the grounded conducting-sheath endpoint mu B_wall + q_i * 0 V. H >= E_wall opens that path. The first forbidden segment gives the turning Z by linear interpolation.
loss.corners: Index = 4*z_side + 2*v_side + mu_side. Side 0 means the lower physical face, side 1 the upper. Center probes use the midpoint of each mapped cell. No population weighting.
loss.display: The route reveal is exhibit time within one frozen snapshot. Point energies and wall access do not represent a time-resolved orbit or particle flux. The cut-cell detail plots native traces within 0.020 m of the right crest on an independent linear energy axis in keV.

entrance.quantities: Only trapped corner of the inner-slope cut cell and native ion multiplier. Physical axial position (m), signed velocity (m/s), magnetic moment (keV/T), H and U (keV).

grid.sampling: 401 native axial Z nodes checked against both traces of the coordinate map. B(Z) interpolates the continuous corner-field P1 traces in physical metres. The independent surface diagnostic agrees with the field at left faces to 2 nT.
grid.comparison: The uniform reference resamples B(Z) in 400 equal physical cells with the same endpoints. For each cell variation sums absolute field increments across all interior native faces. A probe within 1 pm of a face uses the cell on its right. Width in mm is 1000*(Zright-Zleft).
grid.display: Motion between the two grids diagrams cell placement at fixed B(Z). The mapped grid remains static in the simulation. The local face magnifier has a physical Z ruler.

velocity_grid.provenance: The asset records its diagnostic sources, dimensions, transformations and verification.

prints.conversion: Full original single-page PDFs rasterized without cropping at 1536 pixels on the long edge with pdftoppm. RGB PNGs retain the published axes and scales.

figures.quantity: Constant-energy contours in the published magnetic-only model B(ℓ)=ℓ⁶, μ=m=1, H=0.1 through 0.6 in model units.
Published Maxwellian baseline geometry. The physical and computational rulers locate the same field crest.
